title: The Global English Style Guide: Writing Clear, Translatable Documentation for a Global Market
author: John R. Kohl
version: guideline text fetched from the Internet Archive and the SAS sample chapter, 2026-07-18

record.source: Four constructions that close a second reading: a modifier placed against the word it changes, a pronoun or `this` with one referent, a noun string broken into a clause, and a clause that keeps its verb. The installed `technical-writing` skill carried them as one section and named this guide as their source. That skill is deleted in the same iteration, so the four sentences now reach the repository through the principle that owns their mechanism.
record.kept: The four sentences as the installed skill wrote them, with its worked pairs: "only fails on growth" and "fails only on growth", the proto import budget script, and the dropped verb in "Phase 1 moves the converters and Phase 2 the runtime".
record.rewritten: Nothing inside a sentence. The section's bullet list becomes four paragraphs in the principle's body, so each sits beside the attachment failure it fixes.
record.added: The provenance line in the principle, which names this record.
record.dropped: The guide's wider coverage, which the installed skill also dropped: idioms and Latin abbreviations, sentence length, and the article-in-a-series rule.
